editorial.headline: The Ground Work That Keeps Air Travel Moving
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the airport services behind a safe, orderly aircraft turnaround—from passenger handling to cargo, post and ground technical support.
editorial.body:
A foreign-owned company can register this activity in Bali today. It is nationally open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, and Bali does not block it under the provincial PMA moratorium. That matters because this is not a peripheral airport service: it is the operational work that connects an aircraft’s arrival, turnaround and departure to passengers, baggage, freight and post.

Its scope is broad but coherent. It includes technical and operational support for aircraft on the ground, including refuelling, water provision, waste handling and aircraft movement. It also covers the passenger-facing rhythm of an airport—check-in, boarding and transit—alongside loading and unloading baggage, cargo and post. Cargo work extends to inspections using ionising-radiation sources, whether radioactive materials or radiation-generating equipment. Documentation, weighing, security and the special handling of dangerous or high-value goods are part of the same operational field.

This activity may operate at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That range reflects the different layers of airport support contained within the scope: some work is administrative or handling-focused, while other functions sit directly inside the technical choreography of an aircraft’s ground operation. The defining feature is not a particular item of equipment or a single customer touchpoint, but responsibility for services that must work together when an aircraft is on the ground.

Bali’s position is clear in the record. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities island-wide. This activity is not blocked by that rule: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The result is a clean alignment between national foreign-investment openness and Bali’s current treatment of the activity. For founders, the practical distinction is simple: the activity is available to PMA registration, while its actual scope remains firmly anchored in airport ground, passenger, baggage, cargo and post handling.
